messages:
maya: heads-up — following the kernel-selection rfc, I ran a small study on live seq-len distributions this morning. key takeaway: two dominant modes at 32 and ~256, plus a long tail.

sam: nice. did you bucket by actual token counts or rounded power-of-two?

maya: rounded to nearest 16 for starters. did quick perf matrix of kernels A/B/C across shapes. results are noisy for mixed batches.

leo: noisy how? p95 spikes or mean throughput variance?

maya: mainly p95 spikes when mixing 32+256 in same micro-batch. throughput looks ok but latency SLOs break for chat workloads.

sam: sounds like we need bucket-aware batching + warmup heuristics. two ideas: 1) strict bucketing (no mixed seq within micro-batch), 2) adaptive padding + kernel probe to choose faster kernel for mixed. tradeoffs?

aisha: strict bucketing is simplest to reason about, but increases batch fragmentation and can drop overall GPU utilization. adaptive padding helps utilization but can increase token compute cost. also affects KV-cache effectiveness.

maya: agreed. I measured utilization drop ~12% with strict buckets during peak. adaptive padding recovers ~8% but p95 still +40ms vs strict for some kernels.

leo: what about warmup? we currently do aggressive per-model warmup at deploy. maybe we can do tiered warmup: lightweight probe warmup on first few requests to select kernel, then full warmup for hot buckets.

sam: that's promising. define the probe: small batch of 8 sequences sampled from live traffic; run kernel perf for 50 tokens, collect latency/throughput and pick winner. fallback to default if uncertain.

aisha: need to be careful with probe cost on cold paths. it will add latency to first requests. do we run probe in background with async warmup?

maya: plan suggestion: async probing in parallel with serving on a conservative kernel. do quick measurements (<100ms per probe) and then switch routing for that model+bucket when confidence > 90%. while probing, we keep conservative kernel to meet SLO.

leo: what about cache eviction policy? switching kernels may invalidate KV cache layouts in RAM or require reformatting tensors. cost to switch matters.

aisha: true. we should prefer probes that don't require uncaching. i.e., pick kernels with compatible kv-layouts first. fallback to full recompile only if gains exceed threshold x.

sam: define threshold: measured improvement in p50 or throughput that justifies cache churn. propose 15% throughput or 30ms p95. open to adjustments.

maya: also saw weird behavior with very short warmup sequences — some kernels optimize for large context and underperform on short sequences. our probe should sample the seq-len distribution in that bucket, not just average.

leo: for implementation: we need a small state machine per model+bucket: state = {unknown, probing, active, pinned}. transitions: unknown->probing on enough traffic; probing->active if probe result positive and KV-compatible; probing->pinned if manual ops want to force; active->unknown on long inactivity. persist decision in model metadata.

aisha: runtime hooks: kernel-selection service exposes /probe and /decide endpoints. console shows last probe stats. developer can set manual override with api param kernel_hint.

sam: excellent. action items: maya to draft probe workload spec and confidence algorithm; leo to sketch state machine + persistence; aisha to list KV-layout compatibility matrix and switch cost estimates; I'll add a short RFC update note.

maya: logging suggestion — log probe sample sizes, sequence-length histogram, chosen kernel, and cost delta. add trace id to tie to user requests.

infra-bot: deploy: canary of probe service to 2 GPU hosts scheduled for 2026-03-30 09:00 UTC.

sam: timeline: aim to land POC in two weeks, run A/B traffic for 1 week, then decide. any objections?

aisha: none from me. prioritize not regressing latency. :thumbsup:

leo: no objections. one more note — consider opportunistic kernel fusion when bucket is stable for 24h. may make pinned state auto-promote.

maya: good call. I'll include that in spec.

sam: thanks everyone — we'll sync on Monday to review maya's draft.

maya: attaching quick perf snippets here for reference:

```
# probe script (pseudocode)
samples = sample_requests(bucket, N=8)
for k in kernels:
  run = run_kernel(k, samples[:B], max_tokens=64)
  record(k, run.latency_p95, run.mean_throughput)
choose = select_best_kernel(stats, kv_compat_matrix, threshold={p95:30ms, throughput:15%})
```

maya: end of thread.
